'''Katrin Becker''' (born [[Gelsenkirchen]], Germany, October 7, 1967) is a [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and textbook author specializing in [[string theory]]. She is a professor of physics at [[Texas A&M University]].<ref name=":0" /> 

== Life and work ==
Becker earned her diploma under [[Werner Nahm]] at the [[University of Bonn]] where she also received her doctorate in 1994 with a dissertation titled, ''Strings, black holes and conformal field theory''. She was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics|Kavli Institute]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] (UCSB) and then a senior research fellow at [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech) with [[John Henry Schwarz]]. She became an assistant professor at the [[University of Utah]] before moving to [[Texas A&M University]] in 2005.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2019-09-30 |title=Katrin Becker - Faculty Member |url=https://physics.tamu.edu/directory/kbecker/ |access-date=2023-10-25 |website=TAMU Physics & Astronomy |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Katrin Becker |url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/katrin-becker |access-date=2023-10-25 |website=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University |language=en}}</ref> 

Becker deals with string theory, for example in the development of models that make predictions for the [[Standard Model]] and realize models of inflation in cosmology.<ref name=":1" /> She worked closely with her sister, physicist [[Melanie Becker]] (also a professor at Texas A&M), with whom she wrote a popular string theory textbook along with John Henry Schwarz.<ref name=":0" />

A general description of Katrin Becker's physics research has been published:<blockquote>In our quest for the fundamental laws of nature, we are led to wonder how to construct a theory of [[quantum gravity]], a theory that reconciles gravity with quantum physics. Prof. K. Becker works on [[string theory]]. This is a [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]] that predicts gravitation instead of contradicting it and it could be the unified theory of nature. It is a fascinating and unique framework.<ref name=":0" /> </blockquote>In 2003, she received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Research Fellowship]], and in 2005, a Radcliffe Fellowship.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

In 2017, she  received the Bush Excellence Award for Faculty in International Research <ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-30 |title=Katrin Becker - Faculty Member |url=https://physics.tamu.edu/directory/kbecker/ |access-date=2024-01-12 |website=TAMU Physics & Astronomy |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Katrin Becker was born in Gelsenkirchen, Germany to Ingrid and Karl-Hans Becker on October 7, 1967. She grew up in [[Málaga|Malaga]], Spain, with her older sister [[Melanie Becker]], and the two sisters were recruited to Texas A&M in 2005 as part of a faculty reinvestment program. Katrin survived her sister and collaborator Melanie who died in 2020 after a long fight with cancer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Melanie Becker Obituary 2020 |url=https://www.hillierfuneralhome.com/obituaries/dr-melaniebecker |access-date=2023-10-25 |website=Hillier Funeral Home & Cremations |language=en}}</ref>

== Selected works ==

* Katrin Becker, Daniel Butter, William D. Linch, and Anindya Sengupta. “Components of eleven-dimensional supergravity with four off-shell supersymmetries.” [[Journal of High Energy Physics]], 2021(7), Jul 2021.<ref name=":0" />
* Katrin Becker, Melanie Becker, Daniel Butter, William D. Linch, and Stephen Randall. “Five-dimensional supergravity in N = 1/2 superspace.” Journal of High Energy Physics, 2020(3), Mar 2020.<ref name=":0" />
* Katrin Becker and Daniel Butter. “4D = 1 Kaluza-Klein superspace.” Journal of High Energy Physics, 2020(9), Sep 2020.<ref name=":0" />
* Katrin Becker, Melanie Becker, Daniel Butter, and William D. Linch. “N = 1 supercurrents of eleven-dimensional supergravity.” Journal of High Energy Physics, 2018(5), May 2018.<ref name=":0" />
* Katrin Becker, Melanie Becker, William D. Linch, Stephen Randall, and Daniel Robbins. “All Chern-Simons invariants of 4D, N = 1 gauged superform hierarchies.” Journal of High Energy Physics, 2017(4), Apr 2017.<ref name=":0" />
* Katrin Becker, Melanie Becker, John Schwarz: ''String Theory and M-Theory. A modern introduction''. Cambridge University Press 2007, {{ISBN|0-521-86069-5}}<ref name=":0" />
